text.String: Qt shell, primitive-backed 3D, and renderer identity in one authored surface
The new Qt-native shell is carrying the showcase now, and the 3D content is built from the authored Kain primitive library instead of hand-wired one-offs.
This smoke stays inside the native runtime path, surfaces the shared scene contract, and keeps the visual proof focused on a polished product shell rather than a bare harness.
The viewport stays central, but the app reads like product software instead of a test harness.
The clean block primitive used for monoliths, plinths, and stable massing.
The repeating vertical primitive driving the atrium perimeter and depth cues.
Used as a large ring around the central orb to add motion and polish.
The tapered primitive that keeps the scene readable and sculptural.
Cross-platform renderer lane for viewport, swapchain, and debug-draw work.
The higher-level material and lighting lane for polished scene output.
The explicit-engine lane for render-graph control and pipeline visibility.
Staged as a bridge-first backend identity for future device and queue depth.
The smoke app builds through kain-ui-native, launches the Qt shell, and keeps the showcase inside the runtime path.
The atrium scene now composes its massing from Kain primitives so the 3D system reads like an authored product surface.
